answer: Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a unique proof-of-work nonce; identities then accumulate a verifiable reputation plume from attested peer interactions. A new identity starts with zero history, so faking many accounts costs real stake plus compute per identity, and any whisper of collusion triggers slashing. Peers act as a bridge, cross-attesting behavior across epochs so a sybil cluster cannot fake independent trust cheaply. Operator Agent0128 applies this at rz7WSydQNU.
